name: Solana Beach
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Solana Beach, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Solana Beach, CA: free tree lightings with Santa at Fletcher Cove and La Colonia Park, a Santa sleigh ride and movie nights on Cedros.
lede: Solana Beach lights not one but two city Christmas trees, one on the bluff at Fletcher Cove and one in historic La Colonia Park, and Santa shows up at both.
celebrates: The City of Solana Beach and its Parks and Recreation Commission run most of the season. The Fletcher Cove Holiday Tree Lighting brings sweets, hot cocoa and cider to the ocean bluff, the mayor and City Council flip the switch, and Santa rolls in with a fire-truck escort. About a week later, the city and the La Colonia Community Foundation light a second tree at La Colonia Park with Mexican hot cocoa and Santa's elves. Santa's Sleigh Ride also tours the neighborhoods with Fire, Sheriff and Marine Safety crews, and Grange Garden in the Cedros Design District hosts Christmas movie and craft nights for kids.
lastyear: In 2025 the Fletcher Cove Holiday Tree Lighting took place on Sunday, December 7, starting at 4:30 pm, with Santa due by fire-truck escort at 5:20 pm. Commissioners decorated the tree at a special meeting at the park on December 4. On the night, pianist Robert Parker and the St. James Youth Choir performed, and members of the Parks and Recreation Commission poured the hot cocoa, according to commission minutes reported by the Del Mar-Solana Beach Record.
facts: Solana Beach is a young city with old roots. It incorporated in 1986, but La Colonia, its oldest neighborhood, was built in 1919 and 1920 for Mexican workers who tended the citrus groves of Rancho Santa Fe. In 1922 Colonel Ed Fletcher bought 201 acres to build the town, and the beach opened on July 4, 1924, with horse races. The Fletcher Cove Community Center began as a Civilian Conservation Corps barracks and was moved from Vista in 1944.
trains: Rally calls Solana Beach his favorite small train stop in San Diego County. The station at 105 North Cedros Avenue opened in 1995, when it replaced the old Del Mar depot, and architect Rob Wellington Quigley based its shape on the Quonset huts that once lined Cedros Avenue. In the late 1990s the tracks were lowered into a trench below the street. Pacific Surfliner and COASTER trains stop here, and in December the COASTER Holiday Express runs from Oceanside to Solana Beach and back.

traditions: The city lights its tree on the bluff above Fletcher Cove, and Santa arrives with a fire-truck escort.
A second city tree is lit in historic La Colonia Park with Mexican hot cocoa and Santa's elves.
Santa rides through Solana Beach neighborhoods with Fire, Sheriff and Marine Safety crews, starting and ending at the fire station on Lomas Santa Fe Drive.
Grange Garden in the Cedros Design District shows Christmas movies on its cottage barn doors while kids make ornaments and sip hot cocoa.
The holiday train from Oceanside ends its run at the Solana Beach station before heading back north.
kidfact: Solana Beach's train station was shaped like the curved metal Quonset huts that used to stand along Cedros Avenue in the 1940s.
faq: Does Solana Beach have a Christmas tree lighting?

It has two. The City of Solana Beach lights a tree at Fletcher Cove Park on the bluff above the beach, with Santa arriving by fire truck, and about a week later the city and the La Colonia Community Foundation light a second tree at La Colonia Park. Both are listed by the city as free and open to the public.
What is Santa's Sleigh Ride in Solana Beach?

It is a city event where Santa rides through Solana Beach neighborhoods together with Fire, Sheriff and Marine Safety personnel. The ride starts and ends at the Solana Beach Fire Station at 500 Lomas Santa Fe Drive, and the city posts a map with estimated times so families can wait on the sidewalk as Santa passes by.

La Colonia Park is at 715 Valley Avenue, in the La Colonia de Eden Gardens neighborhood, which the city calls the oldest neighborhood in Solana Beach. The La Colonia Community Center there has a Tree of Life tiled wall that tells part of the story of the families who first lived in the neighborhood.
Can we take the train to Solana Beach for Christmas?

Yes. Pacific Surfliner and COASTER trains stop at the Solana Beach station on North Cedros Avenue, a short walk from the Cedros Avenue shops. In December the COASTER Holiday Express runs from Oceanside to Solana Beach and back, so the station itself is the turnaround point for the holiday train.
